publicationNotes: These are concise English adaptations of source-numbered questions, not a full or exact original-paper transcription.
Options retain the source's A–D structure; option wording is lightly standardized where necessary.
The original source has 200 questions; only numbers 1–62 have source-inspected typed adaptations in this release.
The official D-series key accepts all options for Q4 and Q17; these are excluded from scored marks. Q15 accepts A or B.
The official PDF remains authoritative for wording, Tamil text, diagrams and any question-key amendments.

questions.text: Match the 2011 paper's pairs: (a) Salt Satyagraha, (b) protest against the Devadasi system, (c) Neil Statue Satyagraha, (d) The Hindu. Match with (1) Dr Muthulakshmi Reddy, (2) N. Somayajulu, (3) Kasthuri Ranga Iyengar, (4) Vedaranyam.
questions.explanation: Vedaranyam is associated with Salt Satyagraha; Dr Muthulakshmi Reddy with opposition to the Devadasi system; N. Somayajulu with Neil Statue Satyagraha; and Kasthuri Ranga Iyengar with The Hindu.

questions.text: Where is the National Remote Sensing Centre located?
questions.explanation: The National Remote Sensing Centre is based in Hyderabad.

questions.text: Which constituency recorded the highest turnout in the Tamil Nadu Assembly by-elections referred to for 2010?
questions.explanation: The official Series D key selects Pennagaram for this 2010 by-election question.

questions.text: Which of these constitutional articles did the 2011 paper offer for the establishment of village panchayats?
questions.explanation: The official D-series key accepts A, B, C and D, so this item is left ungraded. Article 40 is the Directive Principle calling for organisation of village panchayats; it was not offered.

questions.text: Which numbered World Tamil Conference was referred to as the World Classical Tamil Conference of 2010 in the question?
questions.explanation: The original D-series key selects the ninth conference option for this 2010 question.

questions.text: Identify the incorrectly matched person and description.
options: Surjit Singh Barnala — Chancellor of universities in Tamil Nadu
Fakhruddin Ali Ahmed — Former President of India
A. P. J. Abdul Kalam — Wings of Fire
Medha Patkar — India's representative at the United Nations
questions.explanation: Medha Patkar was an Indian environmental and social activist, not India's designated representative at the United Nations.

questions.text: Who is credited with laying the foundation of British imperial rule in India in this question?
questions.explanation: Robert Clive played a leading role in the early establishment of British political power in India.

questions.text: For f(x) = 1/x² and g(x) = e^(−9x), find the composition f(g(x)).
Which state distributed rice at ₹1 per kilogram under its Public Distribution System in the period referenced?
questions.explanation: The ₹1-per-kilogram rice programme was associated with Tamil Nadu's public distribution system.

questions.text: In what year did the 100-day rural employment guarantee programme come into force?
questions.explanation: The National Rural Employment Guarantee Act was passed in 2005 and the programme began in 2006.

questions.text: Why does the Union government provide grants-in-aid to the states?
options: To maintain smooth Centre–State relations only
To ensure a stable government at the Centre
questions.explanation: Grants-in-aid help states supplement their available financial resources.

questions.text: In which year were seats reserved for women in Tamil Nadu local bodies?
questions.explanation: The official key identifies 1994 for reservation for women in Tamil Nadu local bodies.

questions.text: Which of these China–India tensions were identified in the contemporary news question?
options: A proposed Chinese dam on the Brahmaputra
A Prime Minister's visit to Arunachal Pradesh
China's opposition to an Asian Development Bank loan
questions.explanation: All three developments were included among the China–India tensions referenced by this contemporary 2011 question.

questions.text: On which date did the longest solar eclipse of the twenty-first century (as referenced in 2011) occur?
questions.explanation: The 22 July 2009 total solar eclipse was the longest of the twenty-first century by duration.

questions.text: Qutbuddin Aibak was originally enslaved to which ruler?
questions.explanation: Muizzuddin Muhammad Ghori and Muhammad of Ghur refer to the same ruler. The official D-series key accepts both A and B.

questions.text: Choose the chronological sequence of Indian freedom-struggle movements.
options: Quit India → Non-Cooperation → Khilafat → Civil Disobedience
Civil Disobedience → Khilafat → Quit India → Non-Cooperation
Khilafat → Non-Cooperation → Civil Disobedience → Quit India
Non-Cooperation → Quit India → Khilafat → Civil Disobedience
questions.explanation: The movements began broadly in the sequence Khilafat (1919), Non-Cooperation (1920), Civil Disobedience (1930) and Quit India (1942).

questions.text: A dataset of 50 observations has standard deviation 6.5. If 5 is added to every observation, what does the paper list as the new standard deviation?
questions.explanation: Adding the same constant to every observation does not alter standard deviation, so it remains 6.5. None of the listed options gives 6.5; TNPSC accepts all options and this item is ungraded.

questions.text: A deficiency of molybdenum in soil is associated with which disorder?
questions.explanation: Molybdenum deficiency is associated with whiptail disorder in cauliflower.

questions.text: Which sector was the dominant contributor to India's GDP in the years discussed in the 2011 paper?
questions.explanation: Services had the largest share of India's GDP around the time of the examination.

questions.text: For which of these crops is Tamil Nadu identified as a major producer in the question?
questions.explanation: Tamil Nadu has been an important sugarcane-producing state.

questions.text: Identify Tamil Nadu's officially designated state bird.
questions.explanation: The emerald dove is the state bird of Tamil Nadu.

questions.text: Which queen is identified with leadership in the South Indian rebellion?
questions.explanation: Velu Nachiyar is associated with resistance to the East India Company.

questions.text: V. O. Chidambaram Pillai's Swadeshi Steam Navigation Company operated from Tuticorin to which port destination?
questions.explanation: The route linked Tuticorin and Colombo in Sri Lanka.

questions.text: Which description of Tamil Nadu's economy was selected in the 2011 paper?
questions.explanation: Tamil Nadu has a comparatively high level of urbanisation.

questions.text: Which colour of visible light offers the greatest resolving power in a telescope of fixed aperture?
questions.explanation: Shorter wavelengths yield greater angular resolution.

questions.text: Which graph type was identified as a time-series graph in this paper?
questions.explanation: The official Series D key selects C for this textbook terminology question.

questions.text: The 73rd Constitutional Amendment was enacted during which prime minister's tenure?
questions.explanation: The Panchayati Raj amendment was enacted in 1992 during P. V. Narasimha Rao's administration.

questions.text: In which geological setting does the paper locate skeletal soils?
options: South-west Rajasthan and the Cuddapah region
Telangana, coastal Tamil Nadu and Kongu region
questions.explanation: The source and its Series D key identify the Vindhyan sandstone and Ladakh shale setting.

questions.text: Which pair of Indus Valley cities is a classic example of planned urban settlement?
questions.explanation: Harappa and Mohenjo-daro are the two major urban centres of the civilisation.

questions.text: Which honour was associated with environmentalist Sunderlal Bahuguna?
questions.explanation: Sunderlal Bahuguna received the Padma Vibhushan in 2009.

questions.text: What percentage of ethyl alcohol was the conventional range listed for whisky and brandy?
questions.explanation: The paper's expected range was 40–50% ethyl alcohol.

questions.text: Who introduced reservation for women in Tamil Nadu state government services in the period referred to?
questions.explanation: The 2011 Series D key attributes the government-service reservation measure to M. Karunanidhi.

questions.text: Sher Shah Suri defeated which Mughal emperor?
questions.explanation: Humayun was defeated by Sher Shah Suri at Chausa and Kannauj.

questions.text: In which year did the Delhi High Court deliver its landmark Naz Foundation judgment?
questions.explanation: The Naz Foundation Delhi High Court judgment was delivered in July 2009; later constitutional rulings changed the legal position.

questions.text: Which inscription records a historical confederacy of Tamil rulers?
questions.explanation: Kharavela's Hathigumpha inscription refers to a confederacy of Tamil rulers.

questions.text: Which provisions of the Constitution primarily protect freedom of religion?
questions.explanation: Articles 25 to 28 provide constitutional freedoms relating to religion.

questions.text: Which sector contributed the largest share of Tamil Nadu's gross state domestic product at the time of the paper?
questions.explanation: Services were the largest contribution to state output.

questions.text: Which Mughal ruler was first to develop a notable interest in painting?
questions.explanation: Babur is the earliest Mughal emperor listed; later rulers greatly expanded court painting.

questions.text: The system of dyarchy in provincial government was introduced by which reforms?
questions.explanation: The Government of India Act 1919 introduced dyarchy at the provincial level.

questions.text: Which Indian organisation created the Bhuvan online earth-observation mapping platform?
questions.explanation: ISRO developed Bhuvan as an Indian geoportal.
The numerator is 0.001728 and the denominator is 0.0144; the quotient is 0.12.

questions.text: How many entries did the Constitution's Concurrent List contain at the period referenced in the source?
questions.explanation: The question uses the traditional 47-entry count for the Concurrent List.

questions.text: Which scientist is associated with the development of tuberculosis immunisation?
questions.explanation: Albert Calmette and Camille Guérin developed the BCG vaccine.

questions.text: Brian Lara represented which cricketing team?
questions.explanation: Brian Lara was a leading West Indian international cricketer.

questions.text: The term 'typhoon' is principally used for tropical cyclones in which region?
questions.explanation: Typhoons occur in the north-western Pacific region.

questions.text: Which European trading power first reached India by sea and was among the last to withdraw colonial enclaves?
questions.explanation: The Portuguese arrived in 1498 and retained enclaves in India into the twentieth century.

questions.text: Which is the largest planet in our Solar System?
questions.explanation: Jupiter is the Solar System's largest planet.

questions.text: A relativistic particle has a total energy three times its rest energy. What is its speed in terms of c?
questions.explanation: Lorentz factor γ=3, so v/c=√(1−1/9)=2√2/3.

questions.text: Which of the following passes through rather than cycling within an ecosystem?
questions.explanation: Energy flows and dissipates as heat rather than being recycled.

questions.text: Vitamin K deficiency may cause haemorrhage, while folate deficiency may lead to anaemia. Which assertion–reason interpretation is correct?
options: Both are true and the reason explains the assertion
Both true, but the reason does not explain the assertion
questions.explanation: Both deficiency statements are true, but they are unrelated.

questions.text: Which celebrated Indian painter went into self-imposed exile?
questions.explanation: M. F. Husain lived abroad following controversies over his paintings.

questions.text: Which animals commonly excrete nitrogen mainly in the form of ammonia?
questions.explanation: Aquatic fish can excrete ammonia directly into the surrounding water.

questions.text: In the electrolysis of molten calcium hydride, where is hydrogen liberated?
options: Hydrogen and oxygen are liberated separately
questions.explanation: Hydride ions lose electrons at the anode, forming hydrogen gas.

questions.text: As an economy develops, what normally happens to the share of services in national income?
questions.explanation: Structural transformation commonly increases the contribution of services.

questions.text: Who was not a member of the 1949 National Income Committee?
questions.explanation: Dadabhai Naoroji made earlier estimates and did not serve on the 1949 committee.

questions.text: What is the active dopant ion responsible for laser action in a ruby laser?
questions.explanation: Chromium(III) ions in an aluminium oxide crystal provide ruby laser transitions.

questions.text: What is each lengthwise half of a duplicated chromosome called?
questions.explanation: A duplicated chromosome has two sister chromatids.

questions.text: Who coined the term 'gene'?
questions.explanation: Wilhelm Johannsen introduced the term gene in 1909.

questions.text: For A=[[1,4],[2,−1]] and f(x)=x²−9, what is f(A)?
questions.explanation: A²=9I; thus f(A)=A²−9I is the zero matrix.

questions.text: Which substance yields an aqueous solution that is a good conductor of electricity among those listed?
questions.explanation: Ammonium acetate dissociates into ions in water.

questions.text: Using Brewster's law, calculate the refractive index for a polarising angle of 60°30′.
questions.explanation: The index is approximately tan(60.5°) ≈ 1.768.

questions.text: A horse bought for ₹10,000 is sold at 10% profit and then resold at 10% loss. What does the final buyer pay?
